Build a time frame

Source: R/time.R
time_frame.Rd

The model's time axis is a regular grid of n_steps steps. A step is a calendar month, quarter or year, running from the step containing start to the step containing end. Alternatively, give only n_steps for a plain index 1..n_steps; survey data then carry the time step as a whole number.

Usage

time_frame(
  start = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  step = c("month", "quarter", "year"),
  n_steps = NULL
)

Arguments

start, end

The first and last dates of the window: Dates, or strings "YYYY", "YYYY-MM" or "YYYY-MM-DD", or whole years as numbers. A year or month stands for the whole period: as start its first day, as end its last (so time_frame(2001, 2020, "month") runs from January 2001 to December 2020). The window then covers every step that contains a day between start and end.

step

"month", "quarter" or "year".

n_steps

Instead of start and end: the number of steps of a plain index frame.

Value

An object of class stareal_time: n_steps, step, labels (one per step, e.g. "2020-03", "2020-Q1", "2020"), and for calendar steps starts, the first day of each step.

Details

The temporal prior is a first-order autoregression between consecutive steps, so the step sets the scale on which the temporal correlation \(\rho_t\) is read.

See also

time_index() to map dates to steps.

Examples

time_frame("1995-01", "2024-12", "month")
#> <stareal_time> monthly steps, 1995-01 to 2024-12 (360 steps)
time_frame(2000, 2009, "year")
#> <stareal_time> yearly steps, 2000 to 2009 (10 steps)
time_frame(n_steps = 12)
#> <stareal_time> plain index, 12 steps
